heroHeadline: NRC Closes Comment Period on Fusion Licensing Framework; CFS SPARC Nears First Plasma; ITER on Schedule
heroSubtitle: The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission's 90-day public comment period on a proposed fusion-specific regulatory framework closed approximately May 27, 2026, with Axios reporting the final rule is expected as early as fall 2026. The proposed rule would classify fusion plants under Part 30 — byproduct material regulations — a far simpler licensing pathway than fission, formally codifying that fusion devices cannot sustain runaway chain reactions and produce no long-lived nuclear waste. The development directly addresses a key commercial barrier, particularly for Commonwealth Fusion Systems which filed the first fusion grid interconnection application with PJM on April 28 and is now targeting an ARC plant in Chesterfield County, Virginia. ITER remains on its Baseline 2024 schedule following DG Pietro Barabaschi's historic May 5 on-budget/on-schedule declaration. JT-60SA in Naka, Japan continues integrated commissioning after completing major upgrades, with plasma experiments planned for late 2026. UK Oxford startup First Light Fusion closed a £25M first-close funding round on April 21, with strategic investment from UKAEA and lead from Starmaker One, to accelerate its FLARE inertial fusion concept.
footerNote: Data sourced from DOE/LLNL/NNSA, ITER Organization, Commonwealth Fusion Systems, ARPA-E, UK Government, Fusion for Energy, ANS Nuclear Newswire, peer-reviewed journals (Nature, Physical Review Letters, Fusion Science and Technology), and the Fusion Industry Association.
